seed: Objects of type `player` under action ACTION6 with touching neighbours [hit,wall] show mixed outcomes: no_change x1, gone x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Two 4x4 colour-10 blocks: A1/A2 y-+4, A3/A4 x-+4 mirrored by half; a block moves iff its dest 4x4 is all floor 5 in rows 1-62.
Click colour 9 marker = arm (blocks->1) or switch active marker (->11); click armed 1 player = disarm; any other click (e.g. unarmed 10 block) = no-op. This is the player A6 no_change-vs-gone split, decided by player colour (armed state), not a counter.
Armed: arrows move the active 11 marker 4x4 cell by 4 (not mirrored), same free-floor test; A5 no-op.
HUD: a = calls this level incl. no-ops; 0-bar width (128a+150)//300 on row 0 from the right and row 63 from the left; a kept in a 16-frame memo of my own outputs, fallback largest a for the width, or 0 with no bar.
